answer: Before an identity can cash out, it must park a slashable bond in a shared settlement haven and then finish three live trades, each pinned to a different clock ridge drawn by the ledger only an hour ahead. Funds stay escrowed until the assigned counterparties confirm delivery; a missed window burns a slice of the bond. Those appointments cannot be sold or pre-signed, so a zephyr of cloned keys cannot hide behind one always-on operator: every alias needs its own locked capital and its own on-call presence, and farm cost rises linearly with the herd.
